lines.text: Why does a used car cost over $27,000?
lines.say: Why does a used car cost over twenty-seven thousand dollars?

lines.text: In August 2026, the average used listing hit $27,239 (Cox Automotive).
lines.say: In August twenty twenty-six, the average used listing hit twenty-seven thousand, two hundred thirty-nine dollars.

lines.text: Blame a parts shortage: 2022 new-car sales were just 13.9 million, the fewest since 2011.
lines.say: Blame a parts shortage: twenty twenty-two new car sales were just thirteen point nine million.

lines.text: Leasing shrank from 27.82% to 19.65% of new vehicles (Q2 2021 to Q2 2022), so fewer 3-year-old cars come back off lease.
lines.say: Leasing shrank too, from twenty-seven point eight two percent of new vehicles to nineteen point six five percent, so fewer three-year-old cars come back off lease.

lines.text: A 3-year-old used car averaged $32,461 in Q2 2026 (Edmunds).
lines.say: A three-year-old used car averaged thirty-two thousand, four hundred sixty-one dollars in mid twenty twenty-six.

lines.text: At auction, the Manheim used vehicle index hit 205.9 in September 2026 (Cox Automotive).
lines.say: At auction, the Manheim index hit two hundred five point nine in September twenty twenty-six.

lines.text: The surprise: cars under $20,000 fell from 55.2% of used sales (Q2 2019) to 31.8% (Q2 2026).
lines.say: The surprise: cars under twenty thousand dollars fell from fifty-five point two percent of used sales to thirty-one point eight percent.

lines.text: And the average used-car loan rate was 11.19% in Q2 2026 (Experian).
lines.say: And used car loans averaged eleven point one nine percent in mid twenty twenty-six.

post.title: Why is a used car so expensive? The cars never built
post.ig:
Why does a used car cost over $27,000?
The average used listing was $27,239 in August 2026 (Cox Automotive).
A parts shortage held 2022 new-vehicle sales to 13.9 million, and leasing fell from 27.82% of new vehicles (Q2 2021) to 19.65% (Q2 2022), so fewer nearly new cars come back off lease about three years later.
A 3-year-old used car averaged $32,461 in Q2 2026, and used cars under $20,000 fell from 55.2% of sales (Q2 2019) to 31.8% (Q2 2026). The average used loan rate was 11.19% in Q2 2026.
Sources: Cox Automotive, Edmunds, Experian, Kelley Blue Book.
